direction: Two-condensate reading of NVG (author's F14 idea): the NVG field W gives the U(1) vector boson (omega) its mass, m_A = q_phi W, q_phi = m_omega/W0; it does NOT give the nucleon mass, which comes from the host's standard sigma sector.

declared.direction: Two-condensate reading of NVG (author's F14 idea): the NVG field W gives the U(1) vector boson (omega) its mass, m_A = q_phi W, q_phi = m_omega/W0; it does NOT give the nucleon mass, which comes from the host's standard sigma sector.

rule_primary_gauge.statement: each host's equations unchanged except: omega mass m_omega -> m_omega y; every non-derivative omega self-interaction carries one power of y per power of the omega field (local U(1): such terms can only be functions of |D Phi|^2 = (1/2) q_phi^2 W^2 B.B in unitary gauge, F_munu = 0 in uniform static matter): zeta (g omega)^4/24 -> zeta y^4 (g omega)^4/24, Lambda_v (g omega)^2 (g_rho b)^2 -> Lambda_v y^2 (g omega)^2 (g_rho b)^2; baryon coupling g_omega psibar gamma psi B unchanged (conserved current); sigma and rho sectors unchanged (rho is not the U(1) boson); nucleon mass from the host sigma sector; plus U(y). y from dEps/dy = 0 at every (n_p, n_n) (SNM, PNM, beta equilibrium), i.e. the W stationarity condition.
rule_primary_gauge.NL_energy: eps = sum_i eps_kin(k_i, M_i - Phi) + U_s(Phi) + V n_B + B n_3 - L_vec(V, B, y) + U(y), n_3 = (n_p - n_n)/2, L_vec = A_V y^2 V^2/2 + zeta y^pz V^4/24 + A_R B^2/2 + Lambda_v y^pl V^2 B^2 (pz = 4, pl = 2); dL/dV = n_B, dL/dB = n_3, U'(y) = dL_vec/dy = A_V y V^2 + pz zeta y^(pz-1) V^4/24 + pl Lambda_v y^(pl-1) V^2 B^2; P = sum P_kin - U_s + L_vec - U(y); mu_p = E_p* + V + B/2, mu_n = E_n* + V - B/2. Equivalent (pz=4, pl=2): host with the omega source n_B -> n_B/y, V' = y V obeys the host vector equations.
rule_primary_gauge.DD_energy: eps = sum eps_kin + m_s^2 sigma^2/2 + m_w^2 y^2 omega^2/2 + m_r^2 rho^2/2 + U(y), omega = g_w(n) n_B/(m_w^2 y^2) [eps_V = C(n) n^2/(2 y^2), C = (g_w/m_w)^2]; y from U'(y) = Lambda4 y (y^2-1) = C n^2/y^3; Sigma_R = g_w' omega n_B + g_r' rho n_3 - g_s' sigma n_s (no y' term: y stationary); P = sum P_kin - m_s^2 sigma^2/2 + m_w^2 y^2 omega^2/2 + m_r^2 rho^2/2 + n_B Sigma_R - U(y); mu = E* + g_w omega +- g_r rho + Sigma_R.
rule_primary_gauge.effective_vector_coupling: Sigma_V^mech(n)/Sigma_V^host(n) (vector self-energy felt by a nucleon at the same n); = 1/y^2 for linear-omega hosts; reported normalised at n0 and compared with the refuter's h(x)^2 (passing TW99 points a = -0.02, -0.04, -0.06, b = 0.6)

declared.rule_alternative_mass_only: declared discrete alternative, reported as a sensitivity, never as the criterion: only the omega mass term carries y (pz = pl = 0; zeta and Lambda_v kept as explicit, non-gauge-invariant self-interactions). Identical to the primary rule for hosts with zeta = Lambda_v = 0 (all DD hosts, NL3, NL-SH, GM1, NL-rho).
declared.variant_renormalised: declared VARIANT of the primary rule: the baryon-omega coupling is multiplied by the constant s = y(n0_host) (solved self-consistently in SNM at the host's n0), so the host's omega field and vector self-energy at n0 are reproduced exactly; all omega self-interaction terms kept as functions of the field. Not a fit to stars; the residual saturation shift (from U(y0) and y'(n0), second order) is reported.

derivation.unitary_gauge: |D_mu Phi|^2 = (1/2)(dW)^2 + (1/2) q_phi^2 W^2 B_mu B^mu, B = A - d theta/q_phi; omega mass m_omega y. A local-U(1)-invariant non-derivative omega self-interaction is a function of |D Phi|^2 (F_munu = 0 in uniform static matter) -> each power of omega carries y: zeta g^4 (omega.omega)^2/24 -> zeta y^4 (...), Lambda_v g^2 g_rho^2 (omega.omega)(b.b) -> Lambda_v y^2 (...). Equivalent: the host with the omega source n_B -> n_B/y (V' = y V obeys the host's vector equations). Alternative (non-gauge) rule: y^0 on zeta, Lambda_v.

Equivalent (pz=4, pl=2): host with the omega source n_B -> n_B/y, V' = y V obeys the host vector equations.

derivation.y_equation: dEps/dy = 0 -> U'(y) = Lambda4 y (y^2 - 1) = dL_vec/dy = n_B V'/y^2 (gauge rule); linear omega: Lambda4 y^4 (y^2 - 1) = C(n) n^2, so y^2 - 1 ~= C n^2/Lambda4 = 2 eps_V/Lambda4 (twice the vector energy density over lambda W0^4 = m_W^2 W0^2/2 = 7.44e4 MeV/fm^3)
derivation.softening: Sigma_V^mech/Sigma_V^host = 1/y^2 (linear omega), vector pressure P_V -> P_V/y^2 - U(y)
derivation.no_rearrangement_from_y: y is a stationary field, so d eps/d n_i = partial eps/partial n_i at fixed y (Hellmann-Feynman): Sigma_R keeps its host form g_w' omega n_B + g_r' rho n_3 - g_s' sigma n_s with omega = g_w n/(m_w^2 y^2); no y'(n) term. An explicit g_eff(n) = g(n)/y(n) would instead add -U'(y) y' n to P.
derivation.collapse: U and U' depend on lambda and W0 only through Lambda4 = lambda W0^4 in homogeneous matter (verified: collapse_check)
derivation.uniqueness: dEps/dy < 0 for 0 < y <= 1; for y > 1 U' increases and dL/dy decreases (zeta, Lambda_v >= 0): unique root y > 1 for n_B > 0; y-scans on [0.3, 3] at 45 densities per host confirm one minimum (criterion V and the y-part of G)
derivation.phi_unchanged: no host has sigma-omega mixing, so Phi(n_p, n_n), m*/M at a given density and the scalar ground-state scan are the host's own

key_results.headline: With the author's W0 = 859 MeV, lambda = 1.05 the vector-mass mechanism changes every published host by ~1 percent of what the J0614 tension needs: Delta R_eq(1.44) = -0.016..-0.036 km, Delta M_max = -0.010..-0.013 Msun, Delta z_J0614 = +0.016..+0.036. No host converges; no host passes S in the primary rule, the variant, the alternative or anywhere in the declared (lambda, W0) scan.
key_results.softening_reading: Sigma_V^mech/Sigma_V^host normalised at n0 (= y(n0)^2/y(n)^2 for linear-omega hosts): softening 0.09-0.18 % at 2 n0, 0.20-0.48 % at 3 n0, 0.32-0.89 % at 4 n0 (TW99 0.14 / 0.34 / 0.59 %), rising monotonically to 0.9-3.5 % at 8 n0. The back-of-envelope '0.3-1.2 % at 2-4 n0' is about 2x too large at 2-3 n0.
key_results.refuter_comparison_reading: Same quantity (effective coupling ratio vs n0): the refuter's passing points need h^2 = 1 - (0.75..2.25 %) at 2 n0, 1 - (1.1..3.4 %) at 3 n0, recovering to 1 - (<0.1 %) by 7-8 n0; the mechanism gives 0.14 % / 0.34 % and keeps growing. Decisive difference is in the PRESSURE: the refuter's dip lowers the beta-equilibrium pressure by 10-31 % at 1.5-2 n0 and RAISES it by 2.5-7.3 % at 4 n0, because in a DD functional P contains n Sigma_R ~ n^2 g g'(n) omega and the dip's slope dominates; the mechanism's y is a stationary field, so (Hellmann-Feynman) it adds no rearrangement term and changes P only through 1/y^2 on the vector pressure and -U(y): Delta P/P = -0.8..-1.1 % at 1-3 n0, -1.4 % at 4 n0, -3.4 % at 8 n0 (TW99). It is 10-30x smaller where R(1.44) is set and has the opposite sign where M_max is set; so it lowers M_max and R(2.07) together with R(1.44). The size match claimed in the hypothesis compares the coupling ratio and omits the rearrangement pressure.
key_results.saturation_reading: primary: y(n0) - 1 = (1.8..3.5)e-4 lowers the omega field at n0 by 2(y0-1), so n0 rises by +0.29..+0.85e-3 fm^-3 (+0.18..+0.55 %) and E/A drops by 0.016-0.059 MeV; the variant (s = y(n0)) restores the omega field at n0 exactly but U(y0) remains: E/A +0.016..+0.059 MeV (= U(y0)/n0), n0 +0.09..+0.34e-3 fm^-3 (+0.06..+0.22 %; P(n0) = -U(y0)). Both shifts are below empirical saturation uncertainties.
key_results.moves_toward_reading: 13 of 18 hosts move toward the verdict by the declared definition (Delta chi2 < 0 and |z_J0614| down) by -0.04..-1.0 in chi2; 5 move away: TW99 (+1.20: M_max drops below 2.07, R(M_max) is used for J0740 and z_R207 goes 1.87 -> 2.15), FSUGold (+1.27), IUFSU (+0.50: M_max 1.939 -> 1.929), NL-rho (+0.52), FSU2R (+0.02). TW99, the only published host near the verdict, moves AWAY.

TW99_detail.reading: monotone softening trades J0614 against J0740: TW99 + mechanism fails S through R(2.07) even without J0614

key_results.scan_reading: no host passes S at any of the 9 (lambda, W0) points. Strongest point (0.5, 700 MeV, 4.8x the author's effect): TW99 z_J0614 -1.97 but z_R207 +2.22 (chi2 13.3); DD2 z_J0614 -3.01; FSUGarnet -2.67; FSU2R -2.69; IUFSU -2.25 (z_R207 and M_max worse); 16O moves by <= 0.02 MeV. TW99 fails at every point (max|z| >= 2.13): J0614 passes only at the strongest point, where z_R207 = +2.22. The result is insensitive to lambda and W0 separately (exact collapse to lambda W0^4).

DD2 at 1e10 formally passes S (chi2 13.58, p 0.093, max|z| 1.84; 16O 6.98) with that broken saturation point; the renormalised variant at 1e10 has no eps-continuous crust match for TW99 and DD2.

predictions_reading.omega_mass: mechanism raises the omega mass in medium: Delta m_omega/m_omega = +(1.8..3.5)e-4 at n0 (+0.14..+0.27 MeV), +(0.74..1.22)e-3 at 2 n0 (+0.6..+1.0 MeV), +(1.7..2.7)e-3 at 3 n0 (+1.3..+2.1 MeV), cold matter. Opposite in sign to the 'dropping mass' scenarios; ~10-100x below the omega-peak invariant-mass resolution of dilepton spectrometers (HADES ~2-3 %, i.e. ~15-25 MeV) and far below the in-medium omega width (~100+ MeV, CBELSA/TAPS transparency, as recalled). Heavy-ion dilepton data (HADES at 2-3 n0, also hot) cannot test it; it is consistent with the 'no mass shift' photoproduction results and could only be contradicted by a resolved positive shift >~ 1 % (experimental context quoted from memory, not re-checked in this session).
predictions_reading.stars: per host: M_max -0.010..-0.013 Msun, R(1.0) -0.010..-0.030 km, R_eq(1.44) -0.016..-0.036 km, R(1.8) -0.019..-0.045 km, Lambda(1.4) -5..-11, Lambda(1.8) -1.6..-2.9, I(J0737-3039A) -0.003..-0.006 x 1e45 g cm^2 (0.2-0.45 %): all ~1 % of present observational errors; the mechanism is observationally inert at the author's lambda W0^4. Absolute predictions are those of each host (table predictions_required_hosts), e.g. TW99 + mechanism: M_max 2.0625, R(1.0) 12.4799 km, R(1.8) 11.8934 km, Lambda(1.4) 397.8, Lambda(1.8) 60.0, I(J0737A) 1.3866e45 g cm^2.

verdict_text: The two-condensate reading (W gives the omega its mass, nucleons get theirs from a host sigma sector) with the author's W0 = 859 MeV and lambda = 1.05 and zero new continuous parameters does not make any of the 18 published RMF hosts converge: S fails for all 18 in the primary (gauge) rule, the renormalised variant and the mass-only alternative (O passes for 16 hosts, G and V for all). The effect is tiny because y^2 - 1 ~ 2 eps_V/(lambda W0^4) = 7e-4 at n0 and 0.3-0.55 % at 3 n0: Delta R_eq(1.44) = -0.016..-0.036 km where J0614 needs -0.17 (TW99) to -3.1 km (NL-SH). It has the wrong shape: a monotone softening without rearrangement pressure, so M_max and R(2.07) fall with R(1.44); TW99 (the only near-passing host) moves away (chi2 11.15 -> 12.35, z_R207 1.87 -> 2.15) and fails even without J0614. The size match with the refuter's 0.6-1.7 % g_omega dip is only apparent: the refuter's pressure change at 1.5-2 n0 (-10..-31 %) comes from the dip's slope through the DD rearrangement term, 10-30x the mechanism's -1 %. Across lambda in [0.5, 2] and W0 in [700, 1000] (only lambda W0^4 matters) no host passes S; reaching J0614 in DD2/FSU2R needs lambda W0^4 ~ 1e10 MeV^4, which destroys saturation (n0 ~ 0.20 fm^-3, E/A ~ -20 MeV) and lowers M_max to 1.7-2.0.

answers.1_moves_toward_and_converges: Mostly yes in sign, no in size: 13/18 hosts move toward the verdict by a hair (Delta chi2 -0.04..-1.0, Delta z_J0614 +0.02..+0.03); 5 move away, including TW99. No host + mechanism converges by the declared criterion (primary, variant or alternative); zero hosts pass S.
answers.2_sensitivity_lambda_W0: Exact: only Lambda4 = lambda W0^4 enters (checked to 0 deviation). Over the declared box (Lambda4 1.2e11..2.0e12, effect x4.8..x0.29 of the author's) the stellar shifts scale ~1/Lambda4; no S pass anywhere; TW99 trades J0614 for J0740 at every point.
answers.3_predictions: omega mass rises by +0.04 % (n0), +0.1 % (2 n0), +0.2-0.3 % (3 n0): below any dilepton sensitivity, not falsifiable by HADES; M_max -0.01 Msun, R(1.0), R(1.8) -0.01..-0.05 km, Lambda(1.4) -5..-11, Lambda(1.8) -2..-3, I(J0737A) -0.3 %: the predictions are the host's own to within present errors; the mechanism adds no independent falsifiable signature at the author's values.

practical_value: A validated, thermodynamically consistent drop-in (vmm_core.py: NLY/DDY subclasses of rmf_generic) for any RMF host with an in-medium omega mass from a radial condensate; only lambda W0^4 matters; the omega^4 term carries y^4 under the local U(1)

Rule of thumb: y^2 - 1 ~ 2 eps_V/(lambda W0^4); with m_W ~ 1.2 GeV and W0 ~ 0.86 GeV vector-mass running is <= 0.5 % at 3 n0 and moves R(1.4) by ~0.02-0.04 km and M_max by ~0.01 Msun: negligible for neutron-star phenomenology

In DD functionals, R(1.4) responds to the SLOPE of g_omega(n) through the rearrangement pressure, not to the value of the coupling: comparing coupling ratios across mechanisms (stationary field vs explicit density dependence) is misleading; compare P_beta(n)

Negative result for NVG: the two-condensate reading does not rescue J0614 with the author's numbers; a non-monotone, slope-driven g_omega(n) (the refuter's construction) is not what a stationary condensate produces
caveats: Hosts are the published sets as typed in round3/rmf_survey/declared.py (validated there; DD-MEX validated by the refuter); conclusions inherit that validation

The NVG field is used only in homogeneous mean field; its gradient term (m_W) does not enter uniform matter and finite-nucleus effects of W are not included in the 16O LDA beyond the changed vector field
rho meson mass is left unchanged (it is not the U(1) boson); a model in which W also gave the rho its mass is a different discrete rule, not computed
